subject: green Sahara
title: What If the Sahara Turned Green? It Was, Until About 5,000 Years Ago

scenes.text: What if the Sahara turned green? It already was, and it's due to happen again.
About 11,000 years ago, rain reached deep into North Africa. Grassland spread, and lakes filled the dry basins.
Hippos, elephants and giraffes lived where the dunes are now. People painted them on rock walls that are still there.
One lake, Mega-Chad, covered roughly 360,000 square kilometres. That's more than all five Great Lakes combined.
The cause was a slow wobble in Earth's axis, which gave the north stronger summer sun and pulled the monsoon rains with it.

About 5,000 years ago the rain failed, in places within a century or two. People crowded into the Nile valley, where Egypt arose. And the wobble never stopped: the green returns about every 20,000 years.

description:
What if the Sahara turned green? From about 11,000 to 5,000 years ago it was: grassland and lakes, with hippos, elephants and giraffes recorded in rock art. Lake Mega-Chad alone covered roughly 360,000 square kilometres.
A wobble in Earth's axis strengthened the summer monsoon; when it shifted back, the region dried out, in places within one to two centuries, and people gathered along the Nile. The cycle brings the green back about every 20,000 years.
